correctness.rationale: A binary order-five de Bruijn rotation class is encoded uniquely by a 16-bit feedback mask whose successor permutation on all 32 5-bit states is a single cycle. The complete search of all 65536 masks yields exactly 2048 valid cycles. Legal cross joins change two suffix-table bits; they are realized exactly by conjugate-state chord interlacement. Split/rejoin descent of differing transpositions establishes graph distance = half the bit Hamming distance between valid feedback masks (also independently verified by all-root BFS in supplied source). Exhaustive independent enumeration of all C(2048,2)=2,096,128 unordered pairs reproduces shell counts (38704,305376,758800,710976,254800,27104,368), ecc counts (5:48,6:1264,7:736), radius5, diameter7 and 48 centers. Fixed mask endpoints imply the only possible distance-7 partner is XOR with 0x7ffe; exactly 736 masks have such a partner, hence 368 unordered diametral pairs. Read actual independent truth-table and Hamiltonian-cycle verifier algorithms, both exhaustive rather than sampled.

value.rationale: Cross-join geodesic length is the minimum number of legal transformations between complete de Bruijn cycles. The entire distance distribution, finite diameter bound 7, the optimal 48 centers and 368 diametral pairs are natural exact invariants of a canonical nontrivial 2048-state reconfiguration graph. A complete finite classification is valuable without claiming an all-order theorem.

limitations: Exact numerical distance census only for order-five binary de Bruijn cycles modulo rotation, no complement/reversal quotient and no general-order formula.
Metric descent is prior and not claimed new; whole-paper noncoverage is not asserted for inaccessible ePrint.
